column1: # Allele definitions for bacillus_mlva25_lista_2006, from Table 3 of Lista et al. 2006, which
# pairs the sequenced amplicon size of each allele with its repeat number. The paper calls alleles
# this way rather than from a formula, so these values take precedence over ref_size and
# ref_repeats wherever an amplicon matches a row. A size that is not in the table is called from
# the marker definition instead and flagged OFF_TABLE.
# The size is the Expected column, the size deduced from sequencing. The Observed column of the
# same table, the size the capillary machine reported, is an assay property and is not used.
# Sizes are exact rather than ranges, because an amplicon taken from an assembly has an exact
# length; a one base difference is a real difference and should not be absorbed by a window.
# One correction from the Methods is applied: the vrrC1 row published as 583 bp is written here as
# 580 bp, the value the Methods gives for that allele and the size measured in Ames Ancestor. The
# three other vrrC1 rows already carry the corrected size.
# Two inconsistencies in Table 3 are kept as published, because this file exists to reproduce the
# publication and neither has a stated correction:
#   bams13 391 bp is published as 24 repeats, while the other twelve rows of that locus all place
#     391 bp at 23; the locus is otherwise an exact 9 bp grid.
#   bams34 is not on one grid at all: 386 bp at 7 and 425 bp at 8 repeats imply a different
#     flanking length from 503 bp at 9 and 581 bp at 11, and 238 bp at 3 agrees with neither.
# The half repeat alleles of bams05, bams23 and bams24 sit off their locus grid as well, which is
# expected where an array ends in a partial unit, and they are published values.
